To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a series of intramolecular triarylmethyl-triarylmethyl cations was generated and isolated and the X-ray structures and NMR spectra of the salts were analyzed.

the title compounds are stable salts of a new type of organic cation in which the charge is delocalized over two triarylmethyl units connected by a hydrogen bridge, and that the hydrogen bridge can be regarded as a three-center– two-electron bond.
the title compounds were synthesized as stable salts, their structures were determined by X-ray analyses, and the energy barriers for hydrogen transfer were determined by NMR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a new series of stable salts of triarylmethyldiarylmethane carbocations, and with their characterization by NMR and X-ray crystallography.
the synthesis of a new class of stable organic salts, which contain a C–H–C+ bridge.
the generation and isolation of a new class of stable organic carbocation salts, which are composed of two triarylmethyl units connected by a bridging hydrogen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the title cations are not stabilized by a three-center–four-electron bond, but by a three-center two-electron bond.
the intramolecular triarylmethyl-triarylmethyl complex is the first isolable pure organic compound with a C–H–C+ three-center–two electron bond.

the intramolecular triarylmethyl-triarylmethyl cation is an isolable species that has a preference for a symmetric structure in the solid state but a preference for an asymmetric structure in solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C–H bridging is a key factor for the stabilization of the triarylmethy-lium cation.
the intramolecular triarylmethyl cation is a very stable carbocation, which is stabilized not only by the resonance effect of the aromatic substituents but also by the C−H···C+ interaction.
the C–H bridging carbocation is a stable species in which a three-center–four-electron bond is formed between the C+ and two C atoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C–H bridging is not an artifact of the X-ray analysis but a true feature of the molecule in the solid state and, most likely, in solution as well.
it is possible to isolate a stable carbocation in which the C-H bond acts as a bridging group.
a stable intramolecular triarylmethyl cation can be generated and isolated as a salt.
